chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us from Ishaq b. Muhammad, from Hamza b. Muhammad. He said:

I wrote to Abu Muhammad al-Hasan b. Ali b. Muhammad b. Ali b. Musa b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them): 'Why did Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, obligate fasting?' The answer came in his response: 'So that the rich may feel the touch of hunger and thus give to the poor.'

key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: fasting (sawm), one of the obligatory acts of worship in Islam
key_terms.مَسَّ الْجُوعِ: the touch/feel of hunger, emphasizing the experiential nature of fasting

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah obligate fasting in Islam according to Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (AS), the Eleventh Imam, was asked via a written letter why Allah obligated fasting. His concise response reveals that fasting serves a profound social purpose: it allows the wealthy to personally experience hunger so they develop empathy and generosity toward the poor. This hadith, transmitted through a chain going back to Hamza b. Muhammad who wrote directly to the Imam, illustrates the social justice dimension of Islamic worship.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us from Ishaq b. Muhammad from Hamza b. Muhammad. He said:

I wrote to Abi Muhammad al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Muhammad b. `Ali b. Musa b. Ja`far b. Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. `Ali b. Abi Talib (as): “Why did Allah obligate fasting?” So, he answered in his response: “So that the rich may feel hunger and give to the poor.”
